method: Re-established the 180 EC curriculum and elective rules from the dated UvA catalogue before reviewing the frozen record. findings: The first two years each comprise 60 EC. The third year has 30 EC of open electives, two 6 EC restricted courses and an 18 EC research project. Compiler Construction and Classical Cryptography are the first two named restricted courses. All first- and second-year units must be complete, and the standard plan reaches 162 EC before the final project, exceeding the 144 EC direct-entry threshold.

The broad UCR option covers programming, systems, networks, databases, algorithms and empirical evaluation, with neural-network work as an application. The mathematical option retains the core and adds dynamic systems, advanced calculus and robotic motion. Four courses and 30 EC differ in each direction, and the choices change the subject emphasis. Both repaired schedules keep 24 courses and six advanced units. A third design or ethics focus would repeat existing content without a separate sustained computing spine.

Rechecked where software development and operating systems are meaningful partial matches. General rhetoric does not correspond closely enough to a computing-specific academic-skills course. Compilers, specialist security, distributed computing, formal languages and the degree project remain distinct.

Both concepts and the 28 external titles and 28 UCR course descriptions agree with the published-source findings and the intended normal comparison view. The selected electives, project-entry rule and note references are supported. Optional UCR research is additional and placed alongside the UvA project.
